source_facts: All organizations, dates, rules, and figures in this case are synthetic and authoritative. Loopline is a municipal shuttle pilot connecting the library, market, and health center. The approved launch date is November 6, 2032. Service runs on Saturdays only, from 09:00 to 15:00, with departures every 30 minutes. The fare is zero for every passenger. Reservations are not required. Library boarding is at the west entrance. Each vehicle has two wheelchair spaces; drivers record occupied spaces before departure so dispatch can identify a full vehicle. The approved pilot budget is $4,800 and includes vehicle hire and driver time. Staff count boarded trips without collecting passenger names. One boarding counts as one trip, so a return journey creates a second count. The review is December 2, 2032. The continuation threshold is an average of at least 40 boarded trips per service day; meeting it permits a continuation recommendation but does not automatically authorize spending. The council must separately approve any extension. Canceled service days are excluded from the average and documented with a reason. The pilot does not authorize weekday service or a fare increase. Dispatch maintains the service-day log and finance supplies the spending total for the review. Independent reader journeys: council members receive only the Executive summary in their agenda email; dispatch receives Service schedule and Boarding and capacity as a printed shift attachment; the grant panel receives Evaluation and funding as a separate appendix. The council summary must communicate launch date, Saturday-only scope, zero fare, and review date. Operational extracts need their own launch and fare information. The evaluation appendix needs the review date even though it also appears in the summary. These extracts must remain usable without following links to the full brief.
draft:
# Loopline pilot launch brief

## Executive summary

Loopline launches on November 6, 2032 as a Saturday-only shuttle connecting the library, market, and health center. Every passenger travels at zero fare. The pilot gives the council a defined service to evaluate rather than an open-ended commitment to a permanent route.

The council will review the pilot on December 2, 2032. That review brings together actual boarding activity and the spending total. A favorable result supports a recommendation to continue; an extension still requires a separate council decision. This summary is the agenda version of the launch decision and can be circulated on its own.

## Service schedule

The first service date is November 6, 2032. Operate on Saturdays only, from 09:00 to 15:00, with departures every 30 minutes. The route connects the library, market, and health center. Dispatch should use this schedule when preparing the shift attachment rather than infer additional operating days from the length of the pilot.

The fare is zero for every passenger. A driver should not quote a trial price or describe free travel as a discount available only to some riders. The authorization does not permit a fare increase during the pilot. Reservations are not required, so the operating plan must accommodate passengers who arrive without a booking.

Dispatch maintains a log for each service day. If service is canceled, record the reason so the evaluation can distinguish a day with no operation from a day with low demand.

## Boarding and capacity

At the library, use the west entrance for boarding. This is the location to give passengers asking where to wait.

Each vehicle has two wheelchair spaces. Before departure, drivers record how many of those spaces are occupied. Dispatch uses that record to identify when a vehicle's wheelchair capacity is full. Capacity reporting concerns the vehicle and does not require a passenger name.

Count boarded trips without collecting passenger names. A person boarding for an outward ride contributes one trip; boarding again for the return contributes another. Keep that distinction when answering questions about whether the figures represent unique people.

## Evaluation and funding

The review date is December 2, 2032. Dispatch supplies service-day records, and finance supplies the spending total. The approved budget is $4,800, covering vehicle hire and driver time. This amount is the pilot authorization, not a commitment to fund later service.

The continuation threshold is an average of at least 40 boarded trips per service day. Exclude canceled days from the denominator and retain their recorded reasons beside the calculation. This avoids treating a canceled day as evidence that passengers chose not to ride.

Meeting the threshold permits a continuation recommendation. It does not authorize an extension by itself: the council must approve any additional operating period and its funding.
